headline_marked: [[Roomba Max 875 seals itself to your carpet]] for 3x deeper cleaning, starting at $1,199
headline: Roomba Max 875 seals itself to your carpet for 3x deeper cleaning, starting at $1,199
summary: iRobot's new flagship Roomba Max 875 Combo features SealForce technology, delivering 35,000 Pa suction and 3x deeper carpet cleaning.
details: iRobot has officially unveiled its new flagship robot vacuum, the Roomba Max 875 Combo, priced at $1,199. This top-of-the-line model, along with the $899 Roomba Plus 678 Combo, is available now at irobot.com.

The core innovation is SealForce technology, which lowers a skirt around the cleaning head to create a better seal on carpets. This directs airflow deeper into the carpet, enabling three times deeper cleaning than without the feature.

The Roomba Max 875 boasts 35,000 Pa suction power, the highest iRobot has ever published. It uses a single rubber brush, lidar, and camera-based vision for navigation and obstacle detection, and can climb thresholds up to 3.5 cm high.

Beyond vacuuming, the 875 Combo is also a mopping robot with a self-cleaning roller system. It includes a new heated mist feature called ThermaMist to pretreat stains and a retractable mop cover to keep carpets dry during vacuuming.

The robot comes with an auto-empty and wash dock that automatically cleans the mop with hot water and dries it with hot air. While sealing tech isn't entirely new to robot vacuums, its combination with ThermaMist and new anti-tangle brushes marks a significant step for iRobot.

A midrange model, the Roomba Plus 678 Combo, also features SealForce tech but has 30,000 Pa suction and 18 L/s airflow. It uses SprayForce to presoak stains and lifts its mop 10mm when detecting carpet, but lacks ThermaMist.

Both new Roomba models offer smart home integration, working with Amazon Alexa, Google Home, and Siri Shortcuts. They are also currently undergoing Matter certification, according to iRobot chief engineer Adam Pope.

This focus on deeper carpet cleaning addresses a practical need, moving beyond flashy features to fundamental performance. It will be interesting to see how iRobot's SealForce compares to similar technologies from competitors like Narwal and Dreame.

headline_marked: [[Blue Origin wins NASA contract]] for Mars telecommunications network
headline: Blue Origin wins NASA contract for Mars telecommunications network
summary: Blue Origin will develop a high-performance Mars telecommunications orbiter by 2028, with the deal potentially worth $700 million. This network is crucial for future Mars missions.
details: NASA has awarded Blue Origin a contract to develop the Mars Telecommunications Network. This deal is potentially worth $700 million and aims to create a high-performance orbiter by December 31, 2028.

Once operational, the orbiter will transmit vital science data, imagery, navigation information, and critical mission communications for spacecraft operating on and around Mars. This network is essential as NASA progresses towards sending astronauts to the Red Planet.

The agency's Artemis program explores the moon, with successful crewed missions serving as preparation for Mars. A reliable way to send information from Mars back to Earth is crucial for these long-term goals.

Blue Origin has prior experience with NASA, having secured a contract to build lunar landers earlier this year. However, the company's New Glenn rocket program faced a setback in May due to a launchpad explosion.

While Blue Origin's CEO projected launchpad repairs by the end of 2026, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman estimated it would be out of commission until 2028. This timeline could impact future launch schedules.
